title: Let evaluation use a bounded workload
trigger: A time-limited trial is expensive to operate or too short for customers to encounter a meaningful use case.
action: Propose an evaluation allowance tied to a complete realistic job, such as one bounded project or a stated number of processing credits. Show exactly what the allowance can demonstrate and when any unused evaluation access expires.
mechanism: A concrete evaluation opportunity may reduce uncertainty about fit without an unlimited service commitment.
guardrail: Model cost and abuse; do not claim the allowance guarantees a successful outcome or make payment automatic without clear agreement.
measure: Evaluation-to-paid conversion; cost per activated evaluator and incomplete evaluations.

title: Evaluate removing the upfront card requirement
trigger: Qualified prospects abandon evaluation when asked for payment details before seeing any real product value.
action: Propose a no-card evaluation cohort with the same meaningful product access and a clear end state. Explain that purchasing is a separate choice, then compare activated paid customers and contribution with the existing card-required offer.
mechanism: A smaller initial commitment may reduce perceived financial risk and increase qualified evaluation.
guardrail: Treat this as an offer change; account for abuse, sales quality and service cost rather than optimizing trial starts alone.
measure: Activated evaluators becoming paid; evaluation cost and payment readiness.

title: Start the trial after genuine readiness
trigger: Most of the trial expires while users wait for installation, data import or another prerequisite.
action: Propose starting the paid-feature evaluation clock at a verifiable readiness event, with a maximum setup window and explicit start notice. Define the event so customers can complete a real evaluation rather than lose time to avoidable setup delay.
mechanism: Usable evaluation time may increase confidence and willingness to purchase.
guardrail: Confirm cost exposure, abuse limits and billing-provider behavior; do not postpone charges beyond terms without an authorized offer change.
measure: Ready evaluators converting to paid; idle accounts and service cost.

title: Credit a paid pilot toward adoption
trigger: A complex product needs meaningful implementation work, but a full contract feels too risky before a real pilot.
action: Propose a scoped paid pilot with deliverables, success criteria and a stated credit toward a qualifying subscription if the buyer proceeds. Explain the credit expiry and any work not included in the pilot.
mechanism: A smaller concrete commitment may reduce uncertainty while making evaluation effort economically useful.
guardrail: Price the actual delivery work; avoid presenting a nonrefundable pilot fee as a free trial or guaranteeing business outcomes.
measure: Pilots converting to suitable paid contracts; delivery margin and scope disputes.

title: Offer an operational refund commitment
trigger: Suitable buyers hesitate because they cannot assess the product fully before payment and fear being trapped.
action: Propose a clear, funded refund commitment with eligibility, window, exclusions and a simple request route. Place the concise terms near the purchase decision and ensure support and billing can actually honor them.
mechanism: A credible way to recover from a poor fit may reduce perceived purchase risk.
guardrail: Requires commercial approval; distinguish partial from full refunds and do not call a restricted policy an unconditional guarantee.
measure: Paid conversion and retained contribution; refund demand and processing effort.

title: Guarantee a bounded implementation service
trigger: Buyers believe the software could help but fear they will not get it configured well enough to use.
action: Propose a precisely scoped setup service with a defined deliverable, customer prerequisites and an operational remedy if the promised setup is not delivered. Price and staff the service before presenting the assurance.
mechanism: Reducing execution risk may make a useful product feel attainable.
guardrail: Guarantee only work the business controls; do not promise revenue, savings or adoption results dependent on the customer.
measure: Paid activation after setup; service margin and missed-deliverable claims.

title: Offset a verified switching expense
trigger: A buyer wants to move but a documented migration or overlapping contract cost makes switching difficult now.
action: Propose a capped transition credit for a defined eligible expense, with proof requirements and a clear application schedule. Show how the credit affects the actual first invoices instead of presenting an inflated generic switching bonus.
mechanism: Reducing a real transition cost may remove a practical obstacle to purchase.
guardrail: Review margin, fraud exposure and eligibility; never imply the competitor reimburses or endorses the offer.
measure: Qualified switching purchases; credit cost and post-credit retention.

title: Use actual assisted-onboarding availability
trigger: A staffed onboarding program has real capacity limits that affect when a buyer can begin.
action: Show the actual next available cohort or appointment window and what participation includes. Explain how reserving works and update availability from the real schedule; provide the next option when a window fills.
mechanism: A real scheduling constraint may help motivated buyers decide when to act.
guardrail: Do not manufacture seat counts, deadlines or holds; confirm staffing and avoid charging for unavailable assistance.
measure: Qualified cohort purchases; missed appointments and capacity-related refunds.

title: Run a genuinely time-limited launch offer
trigger: A real launch period has approved promotional economics, but its conditions are scattered or unclear.
action: Present the exact launch price, eligibility, end date with timezone, and subsequent charge together. Persist the same deadline across visits and remove or replace the offer when it actually ends.
mechanism: A credible decision window may help ready buyers act instead of postponing indefinitely.
guardrail: The deadline must be real and enforced; obtain approval for the discount and never reset a countdown for each visitor.
measure: Incremental paid contribution during and after the offer; refund and renewal-surprise rates.

title: Offer a verifiable access discount
trigger: A defined group has a real budget constraint and the business can sustainably serve it at different terms.
action: Propose a transparent program for an eligible group, such as nonprofits or students, with appropriate verification and a clear renewal policy. Explain the actual benefit without implying that everyone qualifies.
mechanism: An attainable offer may convert suitable buyers previously excluded by budget.
guardrail: Validate program economics and eligibility; use relevant declared information and do not infer sensitive characteristics to set prices.
measure: Eligible paid adoption; verification burden, abuse and retention after eligibility ends.

title: Make a price hold explicit and bounded
trigger: Buyers are interested but worry that rapid price changes will make adoption unaffordable soon after setup.
action: Propose a defined price-hold term for a clearly described package. State what is locked, for how long, what happens afterward, and which taxes, usage or optional additions remain variable.
mechanism: A bounded commitment from the seller may reduce uncertainty about future cost.
guardrail: Model the obligation and honor existing contracts; avoid vague lifetime promises or implying that every possible future feature is included.
measure: Qualified purchases; future contribution and price-hold disputes.

title: Separate cash timing from contract duration
trigger: The product suits a longer commitment, but an upfront payment excludes otherwise qualified buyers.
action: Propose an approved installment option for the same defined commitment. Display total committed cost, payment schedule, any additional fee and cancellation obligations together so the buyer can assess affordability accurately.
mechanism: A manageable cash schedule may remove a liquidity obstacle without changing the underlying job.
guardrail: Requires commercial and billing support; do not make installments appear to be a cancel-anytime monthly subscription.
measure: Qualified purchases and net collections; failed payments and commitment complaints.

title: Reward a completed referral transparently
trigger: Satisfied customers recommend the product informally, but a suitable new buyer receives no clear introduction benefit.
action: Propose a simple referral offer with a real benefit for each eligible party after a verified qualifying purchase. Make terms visible, cap abuse exposure, and provide a shareable link the customer can choose to use.
mechanism: Reciprocity and a relevant introduction may support qualified acquisition.
guardrail: Do not send invitations without authorization or require positive reviews; disclose the incentive where it affects endorsement credibility.
measure: Referred paid customers and contribution; abuse, complaints and early churn.

title: Offer a controlled prepaid consumption option
trigger: Buyers want predictable spending on variable usage but do not need a larger recurring commitment.
action: Propose a prepaid balance or consumption pack with clear unit prices, expiry, refund treatment and exhaustion behavior. Explain whether work pauses or requires an explicit top-up when the balance is depleted.
mechanism: A defined spending boundary may make a variable service easier to purchase.
guardrail: Model liability and unit economics; do not enable automatic top-ups without a deliberate agreement or obscure unused-balance rules.
measure: Paid adoption among budget-sensitive users; unused balances and service interruptions.

title: Create a nonrenewing seasonal pass
trigger: A recurring subscription is a poor fit for buyers with a bounded seasonal job, even though the product serves that job well.
action: Propose a clearly dated nonrenewing access pass with an appropriate allowance and an explicit end state. Show its total price and how customers can purchase another pass if their needs return.
mechanism: A commitment matched to the job’s duration may reduce rejection of an otherwise useful product.
guardrail: Treat this as a new commercial offer; verify access expiry, data treatment, support costs and cannibalization of suitable subscriptions.
measure: Seasonal paid adoption and contribution; expiration confusion and repurchase.

title: Let buyers purchase one complete project
trigger: Some qualified customers need a single substantial outcome and will not consider an ongoing subscription.
action: Propose a bounded project purchase with clear scope, consumption limits and completion conditions. Present the ongoing plan separately for repeated work, and identify when repeated project purchases become less suitable.
mechanism: A purchase shaped around one real job may reduce unnecessary commitment.
guardrail: Define what counts as completion, retries and revisions; avoid guaranteeing outcomes the software cannot control.
measure: Project purchases and later recurring adoption; delivery cost and scope disputes.

title: Sell temporary capacity for genuine bursts
trigger: Customers occasionally need more capacity but resist a permanent tier change for a short-lived workload.
action: Propose a one-time capacity boost with explicit amount, expiry and nonrenewing behavior. Show the combined bill and explain when a recurring higher-capacity plan becomes the better fit for sustained use.
mechanism: A proportional commitment may make occasional expansion easier to justify.
guardrail: Requires commercial and entitlement support; do not quietly renew the boost or extend a quota beyond actual service capacity.
measure: Incremental paid contribution; unused boosts and permanent-tier cannibalization.

title: Include a useful starter resource package
trigger: Buyers value the software but face a substantial blank-page problem before they can get a result.
action: Propose a real starter package of maintained templates, configurations or implementation resources tied to the paid offer. Preview its contents and state what work the customer still needs to do.
mechanism: A tangible starting asset may increase perceived readiness and reduce anticipated effort.
guardrail: Include only resources the business can supply and maintain; do not inflate their stated monetary value or imply finished customer work.
measure: Paid activation and time to first useful result; resource-related support.

title: Restore evaluation time lost to service failure
trigger: A verified vendor incident prevents a customer from using a meaningful portion of their evaluation period.
action: Propose a consistent extension or replacement allowance for affected evaluators, based on actual lost access. Explain the new end date and billing consequences before applying the policy through the supported system.
mechanism: A fair recovery may restore confidence after the product failed to provide its promised evaluation.
guardrail: Limit eligibility to verified incidents; reconcile provider dates and do not silently move a planned charge without clear notice.
measure: Affected evaluators converting to paid; support escalation and recovery cost.

title: Let qualified buyers choose the useful bonus
trigger: An approved promotion gives every buyer the same extra, although different buyers value capacity and assistance differently.
action: Propose a small choice between genuinely useful, costed benefits, such as a fixed usage credit or a bounded setup session. Explain each benefit and let the buyer select one without preselecting an unwanted paid addition.
mechanism: Autonomy and preference matching may make the offer more valuable without a larger blanket discount.
guardrail: Cost both options, verify availability and keep the base price unchanged unless separately authorized.
measure: Promotion-to-paid contribution; bonus redemption, fulfillment and satisfaction.
